open_errors.issue: Neela's narration calls Chathu's forty pages 'Black tacky ink'. Ch 29's reveal, and the clue in ch 13 and ch 22 (F838, F870, F975), depend on these pages being plain ink that is dry to the thumb. Calling them tacky contradicts the twist and makes it unfair.
open_errors.fix: Drop 'tacky' so the ch 16 description stays neutral.

patches.find: They were forty. Neela knew them by their thickness. Black tacky ink, a master's hand.
patches.replace: They were forty. Neela knew them by their thickness. Black ink, a master's hand.

open_errors.issue: Ch 16 recalls Kamalakshi asking at the shelter 'What stops a master writing it again?' and Neela answering 'Chathu never needed to'. In ch 3 she actually asked 'If I hold my own page, can anyone else ever hold me?', and Neela answered with the page rule word for word. She was holding Vellan's bird at the time, not her page.
open_errors.fix: Make the callback match the ch 3 exchange.

patches.find: And at the shelter, Kamalakshi had asked it straight, with her own page in her fist: *What stops a master writing it again?* Neela had said Chathu never needed to. She had not liked how fast she said it.
patches.replace: And at the shelter, Kamalakshi had asked it straight, with Vellan's bird in her fingers: *Can anyone else ever hold me?* Neela had given her the rule word for word and heard it ring hollow. She had not liked how fast she said it.

open_errors.issue: Devan says the queen's letter came 'while you were still in Kodiyur' and that he 'wrote back the same night'. In ch 17 the rider arrives while Neela is on the road ('She's two days up the road'), and Devan writes his reply on the spot, in daylight on the arrow cart.
open_errors.fix: Put the letter's arrival during her ride north, and the reply at once.

patches.find: Her letter came while you were still in Kodiyur. I wrote back the same night.
patches.replace: Her letter came while you were still on the road. I wrote back within the hour.

open_errors.issue: In ch 19 Neela ties Devan's welt-less noon with the arrow sheaf (ch 17) to the queen's visit at noon on the day after the gun (ch 16). Two things don't fit. In ch 16 she did prick late, a quarter hour after the gun. And ch 17 takes place about two days later, while she is riding north (the rider has already come by relay, and Muthu says she is two days off). So the noon Devan counted arrows through is a road day, and nothing explains it.
open_errors.fix: Have Neela account for both the late prick and the missed noon on the road.

patches.find: You'd have stood on the shelf with a sheaf of arrows and a thumb that did nothing. I knew that, and I stayed still.
patches.replace: I pricked a quarter hour late, once she'd gone. Two noons on, I was on a post-horse at a gallop and couldn't loose a hand from the rein. You'd have stood on the shelf with a sheaf of arrows and a thumb that did nothing. I knew that, and I rode on.

open_errors.issue: In ch 9 the iron seal hangs on a peg in the gate chamber, 'since Devan put it in another man's hand'. In ch 4 Muthu wears it on a cord, and F1001 says he has carried it since the hall. Ch 4 also puts the cord 'at his chest', while every later chapter (17, 20, 22, 32) has it at his belt.
open_errors.fix: Muthu hangs the seal up only while he writes, and the cord sits at his belt throughout.

patches.find: It had hung there, Neela thought, since Devan put it in another man's hand in the hall.
patches.replace: Muthu had hung it there to write; it had ridden on his cord since Devan put it in his hand in the hall.

patches.find: The iron seal hung on a cord at his chest, a disc cut with a hill and a gate.
patches.replace: The iron seal hung on a cord at his belt, a disc cut with a hill and a gate.

open_errors.issue: Devan has 'spent three weeks bracing for a raid'. The fleet was first sighted in ch 1, only about three days before the gorge fight.
open_errors.fix: Change three weeks to three days.

patches.find: He had spent three weeks bracing for a raid, for fire on the coast and a quick hard push up the gorge.
patches.replace: He had spent three days bracing for a raid, for fire on the coast and a quick hard push up the gorge.

open_errors.issue: Ch 14 says that 'For eight years' no one held Devan's back. His refusal to let anyone behind him dates from Asha's death six years ago (bible, F189), and ch 27 says 'let no one at his back for six years'.

patches.find: For eight years he had held every back he stood behind and none had held his.
patches.replace: For six years he had held every back he stood behind and none had held his.

open_errors.issue: Devan made the drill at twenty-five (F558, and the same passage). He is now thirty-two, so he has been measuring the hair's width for seven years, not eight.

patches.find: A hair. He knew exactly how wide it was, because he had spent eight years measuring it.
patches.replace: A hair. He knew exactly how wide it was, because he had spent seven years measuring it.

open_errors.issue: Devan says Muthu told him about the grey-cloaked man 'in the gate chamber'. Book 2 has Muthu confess in the kalari pit (Oath of Claws ch 8–9).
open_errors.fix: Move the confession to the pit.

patches.find: That's what Muthu told me, in the gate chamber, after Ittan.
patches.replace: That's what Muthu told me, in the kalari pit, after Ittan.

open_errors.issue: Devan says he sat on a boulder to stitch himself. In ch 14 he sews the wound sitting on a fallen ladder rung.

patches.find: I sat on a boulder and put nine stitches in myself with Kandan's needle, and I could not tell which of us I was sewing.
patches.replace: I sat on a broken ladder rung and put nine stitches in myself with Kandan's needle, and I could not tell which of us I was sewing.

open_errors.issue: Janu's hand is described as 'wrapped in its cloth from the day before'. The wrap has been on since ch 4, weeks earlier.

patches.find: Her hand was still wrapped in its cloth from the day before.
patches.replace: Her hand was still wrapped in its cloth.

open_errors.issue: Devan's left-palm blister is said to come from 'hauling the shed door'. In ch 27 Muthu and Kandan carry him on that door, and it was taken off its hinges while he lay unconscious. A three-day-old blister must also predate the spear wound.
open_errors.fix: Give the blister a source from before the battle.

patches.find: Under her thumb sat the rope blister he had raised hauling the shed door, three days old and tender.
patches.replace: Under her thumb sat the rope blister he had raised on the shelf ropes, three days old and tender.
